meta.description: Daily curated Claude AI skills news for small and medium businesses

entries.title: Notion Opens Workspace to Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex as Native AI Agents
entries.summary: Notion now lets Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex operate as tracked collaborators inside your workspace via the new External Agents API. Teams can assign work to AI agents inside Notion, track progress alongside humans, and connect results to live databases — all from one interface. For SMB owners: this means your Claude skills can now read and write directly to your Notion project docs, CRM notes, and company wiki without any copy-paste. Assign a Claude task to research competitors, and the output lands in your Notion database automatically.

entries.title: Inside Anthropic's Own Finance Team: 150 Claude Skills for Reconciliation, FP&A, ERP Migration, and Reporting
entries.summary: Anthropic's finance team runs ~150 shared Claude Skills across reconciliation (AR sub-ledger to GL matching in seconds), FP&A (revenue movers analysis from BigQuery with auto slide decks), ERP migration (validated historical data in 20 seconds per year vs hundreds of manual hours), and master data governance. The key insight: domain experts — accountants and FP&A analysts — write the skills themselves, not IT. For SMB owners: if you run QuickBooks or Xero, this is your blueprint. Start by encoding your most painful monthly reconciliation as a single Cowork skill — no developer needed.

entries.title: OpenAI's Codex Update Lets Non-Developers Build Interactive Workspaces — 20% of Users Now Knowledge Workers
entries.summary: OpenAI launched Codex 'Sites' (semi-private web hosting for agents), 'Annotations' (edit specific cells/charts without regenerating entire files), and role-specific plugins — positioning Codex as an everyday operating environment for business professionals. 20% of Codex's 5M weekly users are non-developers (financial analysts, marketers, operators), adopting 3x faster than engineers. For SMB owners: if you've dismissed Codex as 'for coders only', that's changing fast. The Annotations feature is the real SMB win — you can tell Codex to update one chart in your Q2 report without it rewriting and breaking the rest of the spreadsheet.

entries.title: The 8 Claude Code Skills Worth Installing First — Curated and Tested by the Community
entries.summary: Developer @axichuhai published a curated list of eight Claude Code Skills sorted into three tiers: Foundation (Skill Creator + Find Skills — teaches the agent to extend itself), Product Development (code review, testing, project scaffolding), and Content Creation (image generation, formatting, research). Both Claude Code and Codex run the same open SKILL.md standard, so all eight work on either platform. For SMB owners: install Skill Creator and Find Skills first — they're the 'meta skills' that make installing every other skill easier. The list saves you from testing dozens of random skills yourself.

entries.title: 15 Claude Small Business Workflows Ranked by Time Saved — Invoice Chasing Saves 4-6 Hours/Week
entries.summary: A practical ranking of every Claude for Small Business workflow by estimated hours saved per week. The top three: (1) Invoice chasing — 4-6 hrs/week, reads QuickBooks aging, drafts personalized follow-ups per customer, queues for approval; (2) Lead triager — 3-5 hrs/week, scores new HubSpot contacts against your ICP, drafts first-touch messages; (3) Cash flow forecasting — 3-4 hrs/week, projects 30/60/90 day outlook from QuickBooks + bank feeds. For SMB owners: this is the 'where to start' guide you've been waiting for. Install invoice chasing first if you do B2B invoicing; install lead triager first if you're a service business.

entries.title: Cowork Changed: The June 2026 Shift from Chat to Delegation — Stop Prompting, Start Assigning
entries.summary: A practical guide on the mindset shift Claude Cowork requires: most users still treat it like a chatbot ('summarize this file,' 'draft a reply'), but the real leverage comes from delegation ('Here are the tools, here's the process, here's the output I need — go do the work and save the result'). Opus 4.8's effort controls, Cowork scheduling, and plugin improvements make this shift possible now. For SMB owners: if your Cowork usage still feels like 'AI-assisted copy-paste,' this guide shows how to set up recurring weekly reports, automated invoice processing, and customer follow-ups that run without you typing a new prompt each time.

entries.title: Anthropic Reveals Claude Now Writes 80%+ of Its Code — Engineers Ship 8x More Output Per Quarter
entries.summary: Anthropic published a landmark report showing the AI self-improvement flywheel in action. Claude now authors over 80% of Anthropic's merged code (up from low single digits in 2024), the typical engineer ships 8x more code per day than in 2024, and Claude autonomously fixed 800+ API bugs in April that an engineer estimated would have taken a human months. For SMB owners: this is the leading indicator for what Claude skills will be capable of in 6-12 months. If Anthropic's own engineers trust Claude to write production code autonomously, the same architecture is coming to small business workflows — expect Claude skills that handle entire business processes (order fulfillment, customer onboarding, compliance checks) without human step-by-step supervision.

entries.title: How to Cut Claude Code Token Costs with Prompt Caching in Dynamic Workflows
entries.summary: Dynamic workflows burn tokens fast — a single complex task can spawn 50 parallel sub-agents, each consuming context. This guide shows how to use prompt caching (reuse shared context across sub-agents), scope bounding (limit each sub-agent to only the files it needs), and Haiku sub-agents for cheap tasks like file reads. For SMB owners: if you're using Claude Code and your monthly bill made you wince, these three techniques can cut 40-60% off without reducing output quality.

entries.title: When to Use Dynamic Workflows vs Sub-Agents vs /goal — Don't Burn Tokens on the Wrong Pattern
entries.summary: A practical decision guide breaking down when to reach for dynamic workflows (Opus 4.8's parallel sub-agent mode), when a simple /goal command is enough, and when a manual sub-agent setup is actually better. The key mistake: using dynamic workflows for tasks that don't need parallelism, which wastes compute on orchestrator overhead. For SMB owners: this is the difference between paying $5 for a task that should cost $0.50 and paying $50 for a task that should cost $5 — read this before you turn on dynamic workflows for everything.

entries.title: Boxes.dev Launches Cloud-Native Agentic Dev Environment for Claude Code and Codex
entries.summary: A new startup (boxes.dev) gives every Claude Code and Codex agent its own cloud computer, eliminating the need for local development. Each agent thread starts from a snapshot of your full dev setup with its own filesystem and compute — no more git worktrees, cracked-open laptops, or SSHing into garage servers. Includes a full mobile app and Slack integration. For SMB technical teams: if you have even one developer using Claude Code, this turns your laptop into a thin client — developers can spawn parallel agent threads from their phone without any local setup.

entries.title: Uber Caps AI Tool Spending at $1,500/Month Per Employee — What SMBs Should Learn About AI Budgeting
entries.summary: Uber has capped every employee at $1,500/month per AI coding tool after blowing their 2026 AI budget in four months. Simon Willison breaks down the math: at $3,000/month for two tools per engineer that's ~11% of a typical engineer's comp. The cap mirrors Anthropic's own June 15 Agent SDK credit system. For SMB owners: if a company as large as Uber is rationing AI tokens, your budget discipline matters even more. The three cost levers are (1) effort controls for simple tasks, (2) prompt caching, and (3) subscribing to Pro/Max for subsidized API-usage credits rather than paying raw API rates.

entries.title: How Anthropic Contains Claude Across Products — Agent Safety Patterns Every SMB Deploying AI Should Know
entries.summary: Anthropic published an in-depth engineering post on how it secures Claude across claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork. The three-layer defense: (1) environment sandboxing (VMs, egress controls), (2) model-level guardrails (Claude Opus 4.7 resists prompt injection to 0.1% success rate), and (3) external content controls (MCP servers, plugins). Claude Code's auto mode catches 83% of overeager behaviors before execution. For SMB owners: if you're giving Claude access to your QuickBooks, CRM, or inventory system, this post explains the actual safety architecture — the TL;DR is that read-only access and sandboxed environments are the two things that matter most.

entries.title: Claude Opus 4.8 Launches with Effort Controls, Dynamic Workflows, and Cheaper Fast Mode — SMBs Save on Every Task
entries.summary: Claude Opus 4.8 is here with three big additions: (1) effort controls let you dial down compute for simple tasks and dial up for complex ones — pay only for what you need, (2) dynamic workflows in Claude Code break large problems into parallel sub-agents that run simultaneously, and (3) fast mode is now 3x cheaper while running 2.5x faster. For SMB owners: effort controls are the sleeper hit — set 'low effort' on routine tasks like drafting emails or summarizing documents and you'll use fewer tokens per request. Dynamic workflows mean you can now ask Claude to research 20 competitors, analyze 200 customer reviews, or audit an entire codebase in one command instead of 20 separate prompts.

entries.title: Claude Agent SDK Gets Monthly Credit Beginning June 15 — $20/mo for Pro, $100/mo for Max, Free for Subscribers
entries.summary: Starting June 15, Claude Agent SDK, claude -p, and third-party Agent SDK apps no longer count against your plan's chat usage limits. Instead, eligible plans get a separate monthly credit: Pro gets $20, Max 5x gets $100, Max 20x gets $200, Team gets $20–$100 per seat. For SMB owners: this is a direct cost reduction if you run any automated workflows — your bot that checks inventory daily, your marketing report generator, your customer follow-up scraper — they all move to a separate budget that doesn't compete with your interactive Claude use. Opt in once and it refreshes monthly.

entries.title: Dynamic Workflows Explained: How Opus 4.8 Runs Hundreds of Parallel Sub-Agents for Massive Analysis Tasks
entries.summary: A deep-dive guide on Opus 4.8's orchestrator-subagent model that breaks work into parallel tasks and reassembles results. The three-layer architecture (Orchestrator → Sub-Agents → Tools) means a single prompt can spawn 5 research agents or 50 — the orchestrator decides at runtime based on task scope. For SMB owners: this is the architecture behind 'analyze my entire Q2' type commands. If you run an agency, you can now have Claude research 30 local competitors simultaneously and synthesize a competitive analysis in minutes instead of hours.

entries.title: Custom Claude Marketing Skills: How to Wire Live Campaign Data into Agent Skills for Attribution, Budget Pacing, and Reporting
entries.summary: A practical guide for building Claude Agent Skills that connect to live marketing data warehouses, enforce attribution rules, and answer questions like 'What's our actual CAC for enterprise accounts in EMEA this month, broken out by channel?' The guide covers the exact system prompt patterns, unified schema requirements, and three production deployment patterns (ad-hoc query agents, scheduled insight bots, pre-launch campaign governance). For SMB marketing owners: this shows you how to build a marketing analyst skill that doesn't hallucinate — it reads your actual campaign data and applies your specific attribution model every time.

entries.title: Claude for Small Business Plugin Pack: Complete Setup Guide for All 31 Skills in Cowork
entries.summary: A step-by-step setup walkthrough for Anthropic's 31 built-in small business skills in Claude Cowork, covering the exact installation process, which QuickBooks/HubSpot connections to configure first, and how to customize individual skill behaviors for your specific business. For SMB owners: this removes the friction of getting started — follow along and you'll have payroll forecasting, cash management, contract review, and overdue invoice chasing running in under 30 minutes. The guide also covers which skills to pair together for maximum efficiency (e.g., cash management + overdue invoicing as a weekly routine).
